summary.headline: Exato Technologies FY26 revenue rose about 35% to Rs 168 crore and PAT about 67% to Rs 16.09 crore, with management guiding 50-60% growth for FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew about 35% to Rs 168 crore and PAT grew about 67% to Rs 16.09 crore, with PAT margin up from 7.77% to 9.58%. Q4 EBITDA margin fell, which management attributed to heavy investment in US and Australia hiring, travel, events and leadership additions. Management said the order book closed at about Rs 600 crore (up from about Rs 520 crore in December), and it is pivoting toward international markets, AI-as-a-service, ERP and an infrastructure (hardware) line. Q4 showed a sharp rise in purchase of software and hardware, which analysts questioned as margin-diluting.

financial_highlights.metric: Purchase of software and hardware as % of revenue (Q4)
financial_highlights.change: vs about 67% in prior period (as stated by analyst)
up from about Rs 60-65 crore last year

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 600 crore (about Rs 230-235 crore executed, about Rs 330 crore pending)
financial_highlights.change: up from about Rs 520 crore in December
IPO funds used to reduce debt

segments.name: CX and analytics (CX as a service, conversational AI, agentic AI, automation, workforce management, cloud ERP)
segments.commentary: Core line of business; management cites 150+ customers and Agentic AI orders from a US and a UK customer. Two cloud ERP (Acumatica) deals closed in FY26 with a significant pipeline; management plans ERP hyper-growth and possible acquisitions.

segments.name: Unified communication and infrastructure
segments.commentary: Management expects this to contribute 30-35% of revenue within 2-3 years and cited larger deals in pipeline; it was earlier a Cisco/HP business, now being rebuilt as a dedicated vertical.

segments.name: Exato IQ (proprietary AI platform)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 2-3% of revenue today; management targets 20-30% of revenue and profit over 3-4 years and 15-20% IP revenue within 3 years. Deployed at HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, TaskUs and a mutual fund customer.

segments.name: Vertical mix of order book
segments.commentary: About 75% of the Rs 600 crore order book is BPO/KPO (including healthcare BPOs), about 20% BFSI, about 5% other. Healthcare orders total about Rs 220 crore, including a Rs 95 crore healthcare BPO deal and a Rs 130 crore contract.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: revenue and PAT growth of 50-60%, described as a minimum; management said it can do more.
Long-term aspiration to 500-600 customers (from 150+) in 3-4 years; growth plan of at least 20%+ CAGR.
Target of 50% of revenue from international geographies within 2 years (from about 26-28% in FY26); export gross margin 30-35% vs domestic 22-24%.
About 30-35% of the Rs 380 crore unexecuted portion of the order book expected to bill in FY27; rest over 2-3 years. Management said Rs 120-125 crore of billing is secured for 3 years.
Aspiration to move to mainboard within 3 years and a stated aspiration for NASDAQ; Rs 500 crore revenue target in 2 years cited, with formal announcement of organic/inorganic moves pending under NDA.
Sales cycle of 3-4 months; management expects return on US, Australia and leadership investments in 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Three-day operating plan held across geographies; business solutions built on OEM partnerships (NICE, Mitel treasury for BFSI, Acumatica ERP).
Subsidiaries: US (Exato.ai Inc), Australia (new in FY26), Singapore, and Exato Infotech (telecom/cloud hosting); four in total, three international.
Over 10 delivery locations in India; centres of excellence being built for AI practice.
Management is building an infrastructure practice (hardware and software resale) and a planned inorganic route via a system integrator or product company; 3-4 companies in talks, early stage.
Acquisition plans in ERP and services being evaluated; management said due diligence will precede any deal.
demand_pricing: Q4 hardware and software purchases rose to about 81% of revenue per analyst; management attributed this to AI infrastructure deals and customers using IT budgets before Q4 lapse, with low margin on one-time hardware/software resale.
A $10 million healthcare BPO deal (US, closed September) was cited; consultant said it would have been $25 million if closed in the US.
Management expects BPO/KPO and healthcare to remain the core verticals; BFSI (insurance) is a focus.
Global AI-as-a-service market cited at 31% CAGR; India AI market about 30% CAGR (management claim, no source given).
Middle East expansion on hold due to geopolitical tensions; APAC and Middle East strategy under development.

qa_highlights.question: Why did purchases of software and hardware rise to about 81% of revenue from 67%, and why is it expensed rather than capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI infrastructure deals and customers spending IT budgets in Q4 drove higher resale purchases; these are sold to customers, so they cannot be capitalised. Hardware margins are lower on transactional deals, and a dedicated infrastructure vertical with OEMs (HP, Cisco) is intended to improve margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY26 revenue and PAT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 50-60% growth in both revenue and PAT, calling it the minimum, driven by international geographies, bigger deal sizes and hybrid delivery.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is from exports, and how does margin differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 28-30% of FY26 revenue per management; target 50-55% in two years. Gross margin is 22-24% domestic and 30-35% international.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 380 crore unexecuted order book will bill in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30-35% of the Rs 380 crore will be billed in FY27, with the rest over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan and timeline to grow from 150 to 500-600 customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Target set at 3-4 years, supported by an inside sales team of about 20 people, a US senior hire from Tata Communications, and a planned event with about 2,500 customer database contacts.

qa_highlights.question: What are the customer and order book breakup, and is the 60% international target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the Rs 600 crore order book is BPO/KPO, 20% BFSI, 5% other. Management said 50-60% international revenue is a 2-3 year target, with US, Singapore and Australia push; FY26 international share was about 24% per the management's own statement on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the shareholder base declined and how is investor engagement being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lock-in exits and profit booking are typical after listing (listed 5 December), that some key investors increased stakes, and that PR agency and occasional monthly investor calls are in place.

risks_watch: Margin dilution from hardware/software resale and infrastructure push; Q4 EBITDA margin fell and the purchase share rose to about 81% of revenue.
Inconsistent export-share figures across the call (23%, 24%, 26-27%, 28-30%); FY26 international share needs verification against filed results.
Cash flow and working capital strain from rapid expansion, large orders and a people build-out; management called cash flow the main challenge.
Execution of the Rs 380 crore unexecuted order book and whether Rs 330 crore pending converts within the stated timeline.
Management claims about 500-600 customers and 50% international revenue within 2 years are aggressive versus current base.
Thin stock liquidity and declining shareholder count cited by investors; no concrete investor-relations action announced.
Upcoming AI partnership with a large global company (under NDA) and planned acquisitions are unannounced; no named counterparties.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, international expansion and AI; repeatedly deferred specifics (acquisitions, AI partner, Rs 500 crore timing) citing NDA. Defensive on the Q4 margin fall and the rise in hardware/software purchases, which were explained as strategic. Several answers on export share and the 60% international target were inconsistent or evasive.
key_quotes: We are expecting an increase of 50 to 60% on both the revenue side and the PAT side.
We have an order book of 600 crore.
We already closed a 172-crore managed-services deal on 31st March.
As a listed company, our focus is going to be on PAT.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue and PAT growth of 50-60% (midpoint 55%), backed by a Rs 600 crore order book with about Rs 330-380 crore unexecuted (figures conflict) and Rs 120-125 crore secured for 3 years; no specific new capacity was quantified, and the international, infrastructure and IP targets are not yet backed by capacity numbers.
